(Brisbane, Queensland) | college = [[New Mexico Lobos men's basketball|New Mexico]] (2010–2014) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = *First team All-[[Mountain West Conference|MWC]] (2014) *MWC All-Tournament Team (2013) | medaltemplates = {{MedalSport | Men’s [[basketball]]}} {{MedalCountry|{{flagu|Australia}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[Summer Universiade]]}} {{MedalSilver| [[Basketball at the 2013 Summer Universiade|2013 Kazan]] | [[Australia men's national basketball team|Team competition]]}} }} '''Cameron David Bairstow''' (born 7 December 1990) is an Australian basketball player who recently completed his college career for the [[New Mexico Lobos men's basketball|University of New Mexico]] following the [[2013–14 New Mexico Lobos men's basketball team|2013–14 season]]. ==Early life== Bairstow was born and raised in Brisbane where he attended high school at [[Anglican Church Grammar School]]. He graduated from "Churchie" in 2008. ===Junior career=== In 2009 and 2010, he attended the [[Australian Institute of Sport]] (AIS) in Canberra, playing for them in the [[South East Australian Basketball League]] (SEABL). In 2010, he was a member of the 2010 SEABL Select Team that visited Qatar.{{cite web | url=http://www.golobos.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=209076498 | title=#41 Cameron Bairstow | work=GoLobos.com | accessdate=4 March 2014}} Bairstow was a member of the Queensland team that won the 2009 Under 20 Australian national championship and he played on the Australian Under 19 team that took the 2009 FIBA Oceania title in Saipan.{{cite web | url=http://www.basketball.net.au/australia-reigns-at-fiba-oceania-tournament/ | title=AUSTRALIA REIGNS AT FIBA OCEANIA TOURNAMENT | work=Basketball.net.au | date=27 June 2009 | accessdate=4 March 2014}} ==College career== Following the 2010 SEABL season, Bairstow moved to the United States to attend the [[University of New Mexico]]. In his freshman season, he played sparingly for the 22–13 Lobos. In a team with notable players like [[Drew Gordon]] and [[Tony Snell (basketball)|Tony Snell]], Bairstow showed a lot of potential with his play in four postseason games. In 31 games, he averaged 2.6 points and 1.8 rebounds in 9.7 minutes per game.{{cite web | url=http://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/cameron-bairstow-1.html | title=Cameron Bairstow Stats | work=Sports-Reference.com | accessdate=4 March 2014}} In his sophomore season, both his minutes and production increased after more opportunities. Fellow Australian Hugh Greenwood joined the Lobos for his freshman season in 2011–12 – Bairstow and Greenwood were teammates at the AIS in 2009 and 2010. In 34 games, he averaged 3.7 points and 3.6 rebounds in 15.4 minutes per game. In his junior season, the Lobos had a great season. It was in 2012–13 that Bairstow made the leap from a rotation player to a regular starting five member for the Lobos, helping them win the Mountain West Conference championship and tournament title. Bairstow was subsequently named to the Mountain West all-tournament team, as well as later being named an honorable mention All-Mountain West selection. In 35 games, he averaged 9.7 points and 5.9 rebounds in 24.1 minutes per game. In his senior season, he was named to the 2014 All-MWC first team in what was a break out season for Bairstow. In 34 games, he averaged 20.4 points, 7.4 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 1.5 blocks per game. ==International career== In July 2012, Bairstow was named in the 2012 Australian [[Stanković Cup]] squad where the team went on to a second place finish.{{cite web | url=http://www.basketball.net.au/stankovic-cup-team-named/ | title=STANKOVIC CUP TEAM NAMED | work=Basketball.net.au | date=5 July 2012 | accessdate=4 March 2014}}{{cite web | url=http://www.basketball.net.au/australians-finish-second-in-stankovic-cup/ | title=AUSTRALIANS FINISH SECOND IN STANKOVIC CUP | work=Basketball.net.au | date=11 July 2012 | accessdate=4 March 2014}} Bairstow's 2012–13 season form saw him called into his first senior Boomers squad for the Sino-Australia Challenge against China in June 2013.{{cite web | url=http://www.abc.net.au/news/2013-06-06/boomers-taking-rookies-into-china-series/4738672 | title=Basketball: Boomers name six rookies in 12-man squad to open three-match China series | work=ABC.net.au | date=6 June 2013 | accessdate=4 March 2014}} After he excelled during his Boomers debut, he carried that form into the 2013 Stanković Cup and World University Games, winning gold and silver respectively.{{cite web | url=http://www.unisport.com.au/News/Pages/EmergingBoomerswinSilver.aspx | title=Emerging Boomers win Silver | work=UniSport.com.au | date=12 July 2013 | accessdate=4 March 2014}} In August 2013, he was named in the Boomers' [[2013 FIBA Oceania Championship]] squad to take on New Zealand in a two-game series.{{cite web | url=http://www.basketball.net.au/mills-ingles-headline-boomers-team-for-fiba-oceania/ | title=MILLS, INGLES HEADLINE BOOMERS TEAM FOR FIBA OCEANIA | work=Basketball.net.au | date=10 August 2013 | accessdate=4 March 2014}} ==Personal== Bairstow is the son of Ian and Penny Bairstow, and has four brothers (Kieran, Jarred, Daniel and Sean) and two sisters (Melissa and Stephanie). ==References==
